items.title: Homeowner’s Massive 60,000-Light Christmas Display Dubbed a Safety Hazard by HOA
items.summary:
'Tis almost the season for goodwill toward all—unless you’re Neil Heuer and his neighbors.

Heuer, a semiretired tech entrepreneur, lives in Aero Plantation , an exclusive fly-in community in Waxhaw, NC , with his wife and their children. Over the past several months, he’s been locked in a battle with Aero Plantation's HOA over his annual Halloween and Christmas displays, which his neighbors say disrupt the neighborhood and make them feel unsafe. 

Heuer has been putting on the light shows, which include more than 60,000 lights, choreographed animatronic displays, and coordinated music programming, for the past five years. He estimates he's spent more than $70,000 on the exhibitions. 

But after last year’s shows, his neighbors began complaining. Those complaints led to a hearing, a lawsuit, and proposed potential changes to the HOA’s bylaws that would prohibit Heuer’s Christmas and Halloween spectaculars in the future. 

For his part, Heuer believes the drama has little to do with the lights and more to do with a golf course dispute and a once-anonymous newsletter he penned to bring HOA issues to light. 

"I realize that this is a little unorthodox, but, you know, everybody celebrates things differently," Heuer says of his light displays. "I have friends that celebrate their birthday for the entire month and I might be lucky to have a slice of cake on my birthday, but it doesn't matter. This is my hobby. I love to share it with people. I sit outside and record it myself, and I smile. I'm just so giddy with it.

"It makes me happy, which is good," he continues. "Especially…
items.t: Homeowner’s Massive 60,000-Light Christmas Display Dubbed a Safety Hazard by HOA

items.title: Thanksgiving Is the Worst Day of the Year for Cooking Fires—Is Your Kitchen Prepared?
items.summary:
If you’re hosting loved ones this Thanksgiving, now is the time to get your kitchen ready. Otherwise, a nice holiday meal could turn into a costly and dangerous ordeal. 

According to the latest data from the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) , about 1,139 home cooking fires were reported to U.S. fire departments on Thanksgiving Day 2024. 

That’s a 321% increase over the daily average, making Turkey Day the leading day of the year for home cooking fires.

“People don’t ever set out to leave the kitchen unattended, but a minute is all it takes for a grease and oil fire to take over, and there’s a greater risk of that happening on Thanksgiving when every burner is going,” says Payton Kashani , personal injury attorney, president, and managing partner of Sunset West Legal Group PC in Los Angeles .

By preparing your kitchen ahead of time, you can reduce the risk of fires and enjoy a delicious and safe celebration with family.

Why cooking fires spike on Thanksgiving 

The NFPA says that unattended cooking is the leading cause of home cooking fires. And that’s quite common on Thanksgiving Day.

Many dishes are usually being cooked at once on the stove, oven, and various countertop appliances. Add in a house full of guests that bring constant interruptions and you’re left with a risky situation.

“Thanksgiving fires aren’t usually about cooking appliances going wrong. They tend to happen in those few minutes when someone steps away to greet a guest at the door. Distractions like this can wind up causing serious burns with long, painful recoveries that shake up a…
items.t: Thanksgiving Is the Worst Day of the Year for Cooking Fires—Is Your Kitchen Prepared?

items.title: Spain’s Housing Crisis Sparks a Revolt Against Tourism. Could America Feel the Fallout?
items.summary:
Millions of workers walked off the job across Spain on Wednesday, demanding relief from soaring rents , evictions, and housing speculation. It was the the country's first general strike in 14 years.

In Barcelona, protesters rattled house keys and chanted, “ O baixen els lloguers, o cremen els carrers ," which translates to “Either rents fall, or the streets burn.”

Over the past decade, rents in the City of Counts have climbed more than 50% , with tourism adding pressure on an already strained housing market .

In the coastal city of Málaga, Mónica Reino , 56, has watched that transformation unfold in her own apartment building.

“Every year it gets worse,” she told AFP , estimating that half of its 20 apartments are now tourist accommodations.

Tourism is far from the only force driving Spain's housing crisis. In popular vacation destinations, property owners can earn more from short-term visitors than year-round tenants, creating a financial incentive to convert residential housing into tourist accommodations .

A day after the strike, lawmakers narrowly approved a package of housing measures , including a new 10% tax on qualifying vacation rentals.

The conflict mirrors one already playing out in vacation destinations across the United States, where booming tourism has helped sustain local economies while putting housing increasingly out of reach for residents.

But as restrictions on vacation rentals make accommodations scarcer and more expensive abroad, could more travelers turn to U.S. destinations, intensifying the housing pressures those communities are already…
items.t: Spain’s Housing Crisis Sparks a Revolt Against Tourism. Could America Feel the Fallout?

Nationally, starter home options have felt increasingly scarce as rising prices and climbing mortgage rates compound the challenge. According to research, the national share of starter homes in active inventory fell from 38.1% in August 2019 to 36.2% in August 2026. As a result, some markets have seen a significant shift in their housing stock. 

In Jackson, MS , the availability of starter homes has experienced a slight downturn in recent years, reflecting the broader challenges facing many homebuyers.

Starter home availability dips slightly in jackson 

A starter home is defined by Realtor.com as a property priced at roughly 80% of a metro's median list price, which captures the relative affordability of the lower end of each local market. These homes are typically smaller and less expensive, making them accessible to a first-time buyer or a household with an income at or below the area median.

In Jackson, the share of starter homes was 36.4% in 2019 and rose to 38.6% in 2022. However, by 2026, the share had decreased to 36.3% of the market's available inventory.

Therefore, this represents a -0.1 point change between 2019 and 2026. This slight decline indicates a modest tightening…

The average rate on 30-year fixed home loans decreased to 7.11% for the week ending Nov. 12, down 7 basis points from 7.18% the week before, according to Freddie Mac. Even with this steady month-long decline, borrowing costs remain significantly higher than they were a year ago, when rates averaged 6.24% during the same period in 2025.

So what does this mean for homebuyers? Using the Realtor.com® mortgage calculator , we can look at how the math works out for the median-priced home in the U.S.

All examples assume a 30-year fixed mortgage and include principal and interest only, excluding property taxes, homeowners insurance, and mortgage insurance.

Monthly mortgage payment today with a 20% down payment 

For a homebuyer eyeing the median house price of $430,000, a 20% down payment results in a loan amount of $344,000. 

At today's 7.11% rate, the monthly principal and interest payment is approximately $2,314. This reflects a $16 monthly reduction from the previous week’s payment of $2,330. 

Compared to the 6.24% average from November 2025, which required a $2,116 monthly payment for a home at this price, today’s buyers are paying $198 more every single month.

items.title: A New Wave of Opportunity Zones Is Coming in 2027—and Home Values Are Already Surging in Key States
items.summary:
The United States has thousands of new Opportunity Zones , a designation that could bring rising values to many emerging housing markets.

The Treasury Department last week announced 6,576 new Opportunity Zones (OZ), which will maintain that status for the next decade. All 50 states and the District of Columbia have zones in the mix , and 2,594 of them are in rural areas. OZs benefit from enhanced economic incentives, and they're targeted at communities with the potential to grow.

“By designating thousands of new Qualified Opportunity Zones, the IRS and Treasury are enabling targeted investment and growth in communities where it is needed the most," IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano said in a statement.

This is the second round of OZs since the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act established the program in 2017. The private sector has invested $110 billion in developing the first crop , Treasury said. The original OZs remain active through 2028, and the new ones begin in 2027. Some OZs were renewed.

States submitted nominations from about 25,300 census tracts eligible for the program, and leaders cheered their wins. There are about 25% fewer tracts than last time.

"Whether it's bringing new life to a downtown, creating great-paying jobs, or building housing for more families, these Opportunity Zones will help attract investments that can make a real difference in the lives of Ohioans," Gov. Mike DeWine said of Ohio's 260 new OZs.

“Virginia is ready to harness the potential of Opportunity Zones,” Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger said of the state's 153 new OZs. “I…
items.t: A New Wave of Opportunity Zones Is Coming in 2027—and Home Values Are Already Surging in Key States

items.title: Historic New England City Reclaims Top Spot as America’s Hottest Market
items.summary:
A Connecticut metro known for its insurance headquarters and the Pratt & Whitney aerospace company has reclaimed its title as America's hottest housing market. 

The Hartford, CT , metro area has shot back to the No. 1 spot in October for the first time since a summer run at the top from May through July 2026, according to the Realtor.com® October Hottest Markets report . Hartford has ranked in the top 20 a total of 57 times, claiming the crown eight times.

The Nutmeg State accounts for four of the top 20 markets, with Waterbury, New Haven, and Norwich joining Hartford with median list prices between $400,000 and $460,000, says the report.

The No. 1 market encompasses the cities of Hartford, West Hartford, and East Hartford, but also a large swath of quintessential historical towns that look like they stepped out of a Hallmark movie.

Those small towns—including Wethersfield, Windsor Locks, Avon, and Farmington—draw homebuyers with their small-town charm, stunning nature, and commutable locations.

They also offer relative affordability compared to the elite suburbs dotting the Long Island Sound, such as Greenwich, Westport, and Darien, which are closer to New York City.

The Old Cider Mill in Glastonbury, CT, is one of many working farms still dotting the upscale area and contributing to its small-town charm. (Kiri Blakeley) 

But Hartford, the state's capital, is still close enough that it embraces some spillover from the more expensive areas. If residents need to commute to New York City only a couple of times a week, the approximately 2.5-hour drive or Amtrak ride…
items.t: Historic New England City Reclaims Top Spot as America’s Hottest Market

items.title: Nearly Half of Gen Z Admit Skipping Rent or Mortgages Just To Fund Holiday Spending
items.summary:
The holiday season is an exciting time, but it can also be very expensive.

If you’re careless, festive gatherings, gifts, and travel may leave you in debt well into the new year. 

A new survey by Accredited Debt Relief found that 67% of Gen Z have taken on or expect to take on holiday debt this year. And nearly 15% of Americans are still paying off last year’s holiday debt.

Furthermore, 46% of Gen Z respondents have delayed or skipped rent or mortgage payments to afford holiday spending, compared with 28% of millennials, 14% of Gen X, and 3% of baby boomers.

“Holiday spending should never come at the expense of someone's financial stability, but these findings show just how difficult it can be to balance financial responsibilities with the social expectations and pressure to create a memorable holiday," said Bobbi Rebell , chief financial education adviser at Accredited Debt Relief in San Diego .

"Making tough choices around spending may feel like you’re disappointing those you care about, but protecting your financial future needs to be non-negotiable."

If you’re worried about holiday debt or keeping up with housing expenses, a bit of planning, dedication, and creativity can help you enjoy the season without putting your finances on the line.

Should holiday spending ever come before housing costs? 

Experts agree that your rent or mortgage and related bills should always come first, before you spend money on holiday extras.

“I’ve spent a lot of time helping people who have struggled to keep their homes. And I’ve seen how hard it can be to recover once things get…
items.t: Nearly Half of Gen Z Admit Skipping Rent or Mortgages Just To Fund Holiday Spending

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned after having extramarital affairs with a business executive— Alice Huang , who the U.S. government has determined to be working with Chinese intelligence—and a Nvidia employee. 

Finance chief Colette Kress will work as the interim CEO while the company looks for a permanent replacement, Nvidia said Thursday. 

External and internal candidates will be considered as the company searches for a Jensen's successor.

The news follows a Nov. 8 statement from Huang, who admitted to the affairs. 

“I was unfaithful to my wife,” Huang stated in a previous message to the company. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

items.title: DC Gym Shooter Kills His Building Manager After HOA Dispute Over Mold Issues
items.summary:
A Washington, DC, doctor who had been locked in a legal battle with his homeowners association over mold problems fatally shot the manager of his condominium during a shooting spree on Thursday, police said. 

The fatal shooting incident was reported around 8 a.m. in the Logan Circle neighborhood in Northwest DC, about a mile from the White House, drawing dozens of heavily armed police officers to the area. 

Matt Wade Lambert , 55, a physician living in a penthouse apartment at the Metropole Condos building on 15th Street Northwest, was identified by the authorities as the shooter who killed one and injured four others before taking his own life.

Lambert was suspected of going down to the luxury VIDA Fitness center housed inside the building, locating the building manager, identified las 46-year-old James Stuart , next to the treadmills and shooting him with a handgun from a point-blank range, DC Councilmember Brooke Pinto told reporters, according to WUSA9 .

"Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out," gymgoer James Spellman told The Associated Press . "One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck."

An armed police officer is seen at the scene of a deadly shooting at Logan Circle in Washington, DC. 

Dozens of people were in the middle of their morning workout in the gym at the time of the deadly attack, which triggered an evacuation and an order to shelter in place in the area.

While law enforcement officials have not revealed an official motive for the shooting, Pinto said that the…
items.t: DC Gym Shooter Kills His Building Manager After HOA Dispute Over Mold Issues

items.title: Joanna Gaines Reveals How Her Approach to Holiday Decorating Has Evolved as She’s Gotten Older
items.summary:
Joanna Gaines keeps a beautifully decorated home year-round, so it’s no surprise that she pulls out all the stops for the holidays .

The “Fixer Upper” star recently shared her best holiday hosting tips as she prepares to celebrate the season with her family. She also noted the surprising way her approach has changed over time.

“The older I get, the more free I feel to deck the halls,” Gaines, 48, told USA Today . “I do think this is the one time of year where you can really go big if you want to—or keep things timeless and simple.”

While the Magnolia co-founder encouraged aspiring decorators to feel empowered to go big with their festive displays, she left room for those who prefer to take a more subdued route.

“There’s no right or wrong because the holidays really are so personal and sentimental,” she said. “It’s just a matter of what you love and how you want your home to feel for your family.”

Joanna Gaines is getting ready for the holidays, sharing her best decor tips and getting Magnolia Market ready. (Instagram/Joanna Gaines) 

Gaines also noted that she’s committed to upholding food traditions, using recipes she’s been working on since she and Chip Gaines wed in 2003.

“Food is really at the center of our holidays,” she said. “Thanksgiving especially is this day I feel like I can taste all year long because our family really does make the same dishes year after year.”

Gaines also detailed her approach to Christmas in the editor’s note she published in the Nov. 10 issue of Magnolia Journal .
